title: The Truth About Talent (When Genes Matter and When They Don't)
coreMove: Select habits and arenas where natural tendencies make effort compound faster.
sourcePressure: People differ in natural tendencies and strengths, so habits compound best when the chosen behavior or field fits those tendencies rather than fighting them blindly.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Treating genes as destiny or using fit as an excuse to avoid hard work.

hook: starting with a definition of genes
counterintuition: the problem is not motivation alone

exampleSpecs.domain: a short-track skater choosing starts over endurance events after split analysis
exampleSpecs.audience: an athlete frustrated by generic training plans
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether fit guides where effort compounds
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the coach compares reaction splits and lap fade, then moves her to start-heavy races
exampleSpecs.firstImage: split times taped beside sharpened skate blades

exampleSpecs.domain: a dyslexic founder designing a sales habit around spoken demos instead of long proposals
exampleSpecs.audience: a founder whose strength is live explanation
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the habit fits natural verbal fluency without avoiding rigor
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: he records a two-minute demo first, then turns the transcript into the proposal outline
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a microphone clipped beside a proposal template

exampleSpecs.domain: a museum guide choosing morning research blocks because energy crashes after tours
exampleSpecs.audience: a guide trying to write accurate exhibit notes
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether schedule fit makes repetition sustainable
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she moves research to the pre-tour hour and watches notes accumulate for the first time
exampleSpecs.firstImage: an exhibit placard draft under a gallery lamp

exampleSpecs.domain: a data analyst selecting visualization review over cold-call networking
exampleSpecs.audience: an introverted analyst seeking promotion without copying extroverts
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether strength-aligned practice still stretches ability
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: her manager asks where effort already gains traction, and she commits to weekly visual reviews with stakeholders
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a dashboard mockup marked with sticky flags

exampleSpecs.domain: a chef with heat tolerance choosing grill station reps over pastry precision
exampleSpecs.audience: a culinary student comparing stations honestly
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether natural comfort points to the arena where hard work pays
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: during rotation, he logs mistakes and energy by station before requesting grill training
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a char log beside tongs on a stainless shelf

exampleSpecs.domain: a language tutor with strong mimicry building pronunciation drills before grammar lectures
exampleSpecs.audience: a tutor designing a habit that uses her natural ear
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether fit is used as leverage rather than limitation
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she starts each lesson with sound imitation and adds grammar after the student is engaged
exampleSpecs.firstImage: phonetic cards spread beside a small recorder

skillTargets: identify fit between tendencies and habit design
use strengths without treating them as destiny

tryThisNowSpec: List one habit that keeps failing because it fights your tendencies. Redesign the first rep so it uses a strength you already show elsewhere.
